meta_desc: Step-by-step NCERT Class 12 Maths determinants Exercise 4.1 solutions on evaluating 2x2 and 3x3 determinants, with a free 8-question quiz to practise.

quiz.title: Determinants Exercise 4.1 Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on evaluating 2x2 and 3x3 determinants and finding x from a determinant equation. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Maths, Chapter 4 Determinants, Exercise 4.1

questions.q: Evaluate the determinant of the matrix with rows (2, 4) and (−5, −1).
What is the value of the determinant with rows (cosθ, −sinθ) and (sinθ, cosθ)?
Evaluate the 3x3 determinant with rows (1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6) and (7, 8, 9).
questions.explanation: Expand along row 1: 1(45−48) − 2(36−42) + 3(32−35) = −3 + 12 − 9 = 0. The rows are in arithmetic progression, so the value is 0.

questions.q: If the determinant of rows (x, 2), (18, x) equals the determinant of rows (6, 2), (18, 6), find x.
questions.explanation: Left side: x² − 36. Right side: 36 − 36 = 0. So x² − 36 = 0, giving x = ±6.

questions.q: Evaluate the diagonal determinant with rows (2, 0, 0), (0, 3, 0) and (0, 0, 4).
questions.explanation: For a diagonal matrix the determinant is the product of the diagonal entries: 2 × 3 × 4 = 24.

questions.q: What is the value of the determinant with two identical rows (a, b) and (a, b)?
questions.explanation: A determinant with two identical rows is always 0: (a)(b) − (b)(a) = 0.

questions.q: Evaluate the determinant of the matrix with rows (3, −2) and (1, 4).
If the determinant of rows (2, 3), (4, x) is 0, find x.
questions.explanation: Expand: (2)(x) − (3)(4) = 2x − 12. Set equal to 0: 2x = 12, so x = 6.

faq.q: How do you evaluate a 2x2 determinant?
faq.a: For a matrix with rows (a, b) and (c, d), the determinant is ad − bc. Multiply the main diagonal, then subtract the product of the other diagonal. Exercise 4.1 uses this repeatedly.

faq.q: How do you expand a 3x3 determinant?
faq.a: Pick a row or column and expand using cofactors. For row 1 the value is a11 times its 2x2 minor, minus a12 times its minor, plus a13 times its minor — keeping the + − + sign pattern. Choosing a row or column with zeros makes the work shorter.

faq.q: How do you find the value of x in a determinant equation?
faq.a: Expand the determinant into an algebraic expression, set it equal to the given value, and solve the resulting equation. Many Exercise 4.1 problems lead to x² = k, so remember both the positive and negative roots.

faq.q: Why is a determinant with two equal rows always zero?
faq.a: When two rows (or columns) are identical, the diagonal products cancel exactly. This is a standard property of determinants and a quick way to spot a zero value without full expansion.
